Most harmony "tricks" are **moves**: ways of getting from one chord to the
next while each finger travels as little as possible. Tymoczko's *A Geometry
of Music* explains why so few moves do so much work. Stepwise voices and
consistent chords leave only a few options, and the familiar chords (triads
and 7ths) divide the octave almost evenly, so they link up by small moves.

This map groups the moves by **how the voices move**, not by topic. Start
anywhere, follow a **path**, or pick a **song** to see which moves it uses
and hear its progression.

# The five clusters

Each cluster has a page and a slide deck. The lessons in them are short: an
idea, how it looks on the neck, an interactive fretboard, songs that use the
move, and something to **try**.

| Cluster | What moves | Page | Slides |
|---|---|---|---|
| Space | nothing: where notes live | [Space](space.html) | [deck](space-slides.html) |
| Hold & step | two voices hold, one steps | [Hold & step](hold-step.html) | [deck](hold-step-slides.html) |
| Fifth motion | the root falls a fifth | [Fifth motion](fifth-motion.html) | [deck](fifth-motion-slides.html) |
| Symmetry moves | nearly even chords slide | [Symmetry moves](symmetry.html) | [deck](symmetry-slides.html) |
| Parallel slides | the whole shape moves | [Parallel slides](parallel.html) | [deck](parallel-slides.html) |

## How to read the diagrams

In chord diagrams the dots are labelled by **degree** (R = root, 3, 5, ♭7, …),
colored the same way throughout. When a progression plays, a **gold ring**
marks a note that stays put and an **orange line** marks a note that moves by
a step. Standard tuning (E A D G B E), high E at the top; tick *⚙ low E on
top* on any fretboard to flip them all.

## Drills

- I–IV–V in every key using only the L shape ([Where the chords of a key live](space.html#key-map))
- ii–V–I in shells, major and minor, roots on both strings ([Shells and guide tones](fifth-motion.html#guide-tones))
- Harmonize one melody note six ways ([One note, three roles](space.html#one-note-three-roles))
- One chord, five CAGED positions, up and down ([CAGED](space.html#caged))
- Each secondary dominant into its target, in three keys ([Secondary dominants](fifth-motion.html#secondary-dominants))
